Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood and we can see clear cost/latency wins if this moves forward. Before we get legal involved, procurement asked me to formalize a request for a multi-year pricing arrangement to present internally. The high-level ask: 

- 3-year term
- Price lock at the proposed rates for the full term
- Uplift cap: not to exceed 8% year-over-year
- Renewal protection: guarantee the same cap/discounting treatment at renewal or a credit if rates move against us

We’re prepared to commit to an initial annual spend of ~$1.2M (estimated token-based usage) with an annual true-up. Attached a short SOW and our Q4 forecast for context.

Can Redwood provide executive signoff (or an exception) for these terms? If we can get confirmation this week, we’d like to move to legal and have an order form signed by mid-December.

Best,
Samantha Jones

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: multi-year rate fortification & renewal protection — exec review requested

Folks — forwarding procurement’s formal ask from TerraHealth (thread below). Summary and recommended guardrails: 

External ask: 3-year firm price lock, uplift cap <= 8%/yr, renewal protection clause guaranteeing similar pricing treatment at renewal (or credit). Initial committed ARR ~ $1.2M.

Why I’m escalating: This is a non-standard term (multi-year price lock + renewal guarantee). Deal economics are healthy but the longevity of the lock materially affects future pricing flexibility and our ability to reprice across product improvements and model refreshes.

Recommended concession (sales-recommended):
- Approve a 3-year term with price lock on per-token base rate, subject to an annual uplift cap of 7% (instead of 8%).
- Renewal protection: guarantee a one-time renewal fallback for the immediate renewal period that cannot exceed the uplift cap; after that, renewal pricing reverts to market with a right to negotiate.
- Commit threshold: TerraHealth must maintain >= 90% of the agreed annual committed spend on a trailing 12-month basis to retain renewal protection; otherwise standard renewal pricing applies.
- Payment: annual prepay preferred (provides capacity certainty) — if invoiced instead, require net-30 with credit approval.
- SLA: include standard Redwood SLAs; any SLA credit exposure capped at 1% of annual invoice for the term.

Financial impact: conservative internal estimate shows a 9–11% LTV haircut vs. market renewal paths over 3 years; we can offset with an initial 18% discount on first-year list in exchange for annual prepay.

Ask: Exec signoff (Marissa) to allow Deal Desk to accept the above structure. If approved, I’ll coordinate Legal to draft an order form and the specific renewal protection language.

Attachments: TerraHealth_SOW_v1.pdf, TerraHealth_Q4-forecast.xlsx, Financial_impact_DL-78421.xlsx (internal)

—Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: multi-year rate fortification & renewal protection — exec review requested

Logan — reviewed your summary and the attachments. I’m willing to approve an exception with tightened guardrails to protect long-term economics and avoid creating a broad precedent. Approval notes below: 

Approved structure (conditions):
- 3-year term with price lock on the agreed per-token rate.
- Uplift cap: capped at 6% year-over-year (final decision: 6%, not 7%).
- Renewal protection: grant TerraHealth a one-time option at the first renewal to maintain the uplift cap (6%) for one renewal term only, provided they meet the commit threshold. After that, renewal is subject to market pricing.
- Commit threshold: TerraHealth must hit >= 95% of the committed annual spend on a trailing 12-month basis to qualify for the renewal option.
- Payment: require annual prepay or a signed credit-approved invoice schedule. No net-60 exceptions.
- Legal to draft explicit termination & clawback language tied to under-usage; any credits for SLA or other concessions capped at 1% of annualized invoice.

Please have Legal prepare an order form reflecting the 6% uplift cap, the one-time renewal option, and the 95% commit test. Ben, please run final margin sensitivity and confirm internal finance OK with the revised 6% cap; flag any material P&L exposure.

If Legal approves the wording and Finance signs off, roll forward to TerraHealth with a target signature date of Dec 15.

—Marissa

- Uplift cap: 6% year-over-year (firm).

- Commit test: TerraHealth must maintain >= 95% of the agreed annual committed spend (trailing 12 months) to qualify for the renewal option.
- Payment: annual prepay preferred. If invoiced, must be on a credit-approved schedule; no net-60.
- SLA/credits: any SLA credits limited to 1% of annualized invoice.
